Alex: Quick sync — Optimize advisor prioritization. Customers keep asking for per-route batching hints, cache rules, and quantization recommendations that are safe. Also a recurring ask: eval-triggered alerts for quality drift. Need to agree MVP + launch criteria.
Maria: Agree on focus. Large enterprise pilot asked for per-route batch size suggestions and a simple rollout checklist for quantization. They want no regressions on 3 key prompt sets.
Sasha: Eval alerts are higher risk but high impact. If we can wire simple regression alerts to existing evals, customers will pay for that. But infra needs to avoid noisy alerts.
Jordan: What are our target impact metrics? e.g., 20% token-cost reduction for caching+batching? and alerts should detect >=2% metric drop on core prompts?
Ken: Rough engineering estimates: batching advisor (MVP) ~ 2 devs x 4 weeks (data + UI + API). caching suggestions ~ 2 weeks. quantization recommendations: research spike 2 weeks + 4 weeks to ship conservative profiles. eval-triggered alerts: infra + product work ~ 3-4 weeks.
Alex: Proposed MVP scope (short):
- Advisor API + Console: per-route batching suggestion (static rule + simulation)
- Simple cache rule generator (prefix caching hints)
- Quantization recs: conservative choices for our 3 most common models (with rollback playbook)
- Eval alert stub: connect current eval results -> UI alerting, no automated rollback
Launch criteria (must-have):
- Advisor suggests batch sizes that are validated by simulation and produce <=5% p99 latency regression in our tests
- Cache hints demonstrably reduce token count in 2/3 pilot routes
- Quant recs have eval passes on customer prompt suites (no regression >1% on quality metric)
- Alerting: configurable threshold + daily digest, <5% false positive rate in pilot
Maria: I like conservative launch bars. For quant recs we should require a canary flow: deploy quantized variant behind routing flag for 1% traffic for 48h, compare evals.
Sasha: Risk note: customers will try blanket INT8 on hallucination-sensitive flows. We should make recommendations model+workload specific and flag risky flows.
Jordan: Telemetry/PII question: to run per-route suggestions we need sample prompts. We should support uploading anonymized prompt sets or running an on-prem analysis path. Customers will balk at sending raw prompts.
Ken: Implementation note: MVP will simulate batching using sampled request headers + seq length histogram. Example quick CLI to run a local sim:
```
ri-sim --input sample_requests.json --model gptx-20b --target-latency 100
```
Outputs: suggested_batch=8, expected_qps=120, tail_latency=90ms
Maria: Ops/Privacy plan: default to opt-in telemetry; provide instructions for customers to run the sim locally and upload the results. For enterprise pilots we can run via private deployment.
Alex: Prioritization tradeoffs:
- If we need to cut scope, drop automated quant rollout (keep recs) and delay alerting automation to beta
- If customers push for faster ROI, accelerate batching+cache and ship quant recs in a follow-up
Sasha: Can we add a simple eval rule: mark any prompt set where token-penalty metric drops >2% as "needs review"? That keeps alerts less noisy.
Ken: Agree. We'll implement an eval threshold config per customer and default to 2%. Implementation will plug into current eval pipeline.
